key_insight: The paper recasts phase-field fracture for composite shells as a replaceable, certified constitutive operator built from four orthogonal strain invariants, enabling fracture mechanisms to be separated, degraded, and solved consistently on curved shells.
engineering_relevance: This makes shell-fracture simulation more flexible and trustworthy for fibre-reinforced composites, especially when fibre orientation and curvature strongly influence damage growth, load capacity, and through-thickness asymmetry.
method: Map Green-Lagrange strain through the shell metric Cholesky factor into four invariant channels.
Use channel-wise potentials for tension-compression split, degradation, plane-stress condensation, and consistent tangent assembly.
Certify admissible operators with algebraic, solver-state, and training-data protocol checks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical studies on notched IM7/8552 shells that verify the discretisation in thin and curved regimes and demonstrate predicted effects of fibre orientation and curvature on damage and capacity.
watch_item: The framework depends on admissible operator conditions and positive residual stiffness for stable plane-stress condensation, so learned or custom operators must be carefully certified before use.
paper_title: Mechanism-resolved phase-field fracture of composite shells with a certified admissible constitutive operator
